audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven stages is marked Aurora, in both layers, on a 49.69% win rate over 161 games. A lane Aurora wins at every single stage does not come out at a coin flip, and the packet's own level chart reads Garen for the first five stages before flipping.
audit.why: Decisive Strike (Q, 8s) 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him. His next attack strikes a vital area of his foe, dealing bonus damage and silencing them.' It breaks The Weirding's slow on cast and silences on the hit — a silenced Aurora cannot cast Across the Veil or Between Worlds at all. Before you have items, an 8-second silence-on-demand beats a 22-second escape. Aurora's edge is real but it is a two-item edge, not a level-1 edge.
audit.corrected: The early stages belong to Garen while Decisive Strike's silence out-cycles a 22s escape; Aurora takes over from first item onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and gave no cooldowns.
audit.why: Demacian Justice is 120/100/80 and is an execute that, per the missing-interactions file, bypasses stacked resistances — so MR does not save you from it. Between Worlds is 140s, longer than his at every rank.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his step-up. Demacian Justice is 120s and executes through resistances — MR does not answer it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tracks Courage as the matchup-defining ability, which is the wrong ability entirely, and both layers say Between Worlds lets Aurora 'walk a wall onto him untargetable' (spikes[3].text and late). Aurora has no untargetability and no wall-walk — Between Worlds teleports between the two sides of the zone she places.
audit.why: The ability that decides this lane is Decisive Strike (Q, 8s, 300 range): it breaks slows and silences. A silence is the one effect that turns off Aurora's entire escape package, and it comes back every 8 seconds — that is what makes his step-up threatening, not Courage. Courage (W, 22/19.5/17/14.5/12) is a shield plus tenacity plus a longer damage reduction; tenacity matters if your jungler brings CC, and it is the ability to bait before you burst, but it is not what kills you. Perseverance (P) regenerates a percentage of his total health each second 'if Garen has not recently been struck' — so a single Twofold Hex thrown at him every few seconds denies his entire lane sustain, which is worth more than any trade you could take.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike breaks slows and silences on the hit — silenced, you cannot cast Across the Veil or the rift at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage is tracked without its number and framed as the cooldown to fight around.
audit.why: Courage is 22s at rank 1 and Decisive Strike is a flat 8s. The 8-second silence is the clock that governs whether you can walk up; the 22-second shield is the clock that governs whether your burst lands.
audit.corrected: Courage is 22s and shields him; Decisive Strike is a flat 8s silence — count both.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says that chip damage shuts off Perseverance.
audit.why: His passive only ticks when he has not recently been damaged. A single Q every few seconds denies all of it and is a stronger use of your mana than trying to win a trade outright.
audit.corrected: One Q every few seconds shuts Perseverance off — chip him constantly, do not save it for trades.

edits.after: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his step-up. Demacian Justice is 120s and executes through resistances, so MR is not the answer.

edits.before: With two AP items your Q-out, Q-recast-pull-into-E burst out-chunks anything his Perseverance passive can regen between trades, and Between Worlds (R) lets you zone or walk a wall onto him untargetable — his short Q-E-then-disengage pattern can't win the poke war anymore.
edits.after: With two AP items your Q-out, Q-recast-pull-into-E burst out-chunks anything Perseverance can regen between trades — and chip alone stops it ticking. Between Worlds slows him and teleports you across the rift, so his 8s Decisive Strike silence never catches you standing still.

notes: The level chart is the headline problem here: both layers currently give Aurora all seven stages against a 49.69% win rate over 161 games, while the packet's own level chart reads Garen for the first five. I have written the correction into the point-2 audit entry rather than as side edits, because the side and rating fields are short enums that the length band rejects. The correct sequence is Garen through Levels 4-5, skill at 6, Aurora from first item. The 'late' paragraph also still carries the 'walk a wall onto him untargetable' claim; Between Worlds teleports between the two sides of its own zone and does not cross arbitrary terrain.
